import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from collections import Counter

# Set random seed for reproducibility
np.random.seed(42)

# Load data
train = pd.read_csv("./input/ru_train.csv")
test = pd.read_csv("./input/ru_test_2.csv")
sample_sub = pd.read_csv("./input/ru_sample_submission_2.csv")

# Efficiently create validation split (1% hold-out)
train_size = len(train)
val_size = int(0.01 * train_size)
indices = np.random.permutation(train_size)
val_indices = indices[:val_size]
train_indices = indices[val_size:]

# Use stratified split on 'class' if available to preserve distribution (optional but beneficial)
train_fold = train.iloc[train_indices].reset_index(drop=True)
val_fold = train.iloc[val_indices].reset_index(drop=True)

# Build class-conditioned token mapping: (before, class) -> most common after
token_class_to_norm = {}
for _, group in train_fold.groupby(["before", "class"]):
    before = group["before"].iloc[0]
    cls = group["class"].iloc[0]
    norm_counts = group["after"].value_counts()
    most_common_norm = norm_counts.index[0]
    token_class_to_norm[(before, cls)] = most_common_norm

# Build class-agnostic global mapping: before -> most common after across all classes
token_to_norm_global = {}
for _, group in train_fold.groupby("before"):
    before = group["before"].iloc[0]
    norm_counts = group["after"].value_counts()
    most_common_norm = norm_counts.index[0]
    token_to_norm_global[before] = most_common_norm

# Prepare validation predictions using class-aware mapping with global fallback
val_fold = val_fold.copy()
val_fold["prediction"] = val_fold.apply(
    lambda row: token_class_to_norm.get(
        (row["before"], row["class"]),
        token_to_norm_global.get(row["before"], row["before"]),
    ),
    axis=1,
)

# Compute accuracy
val_accuracy = (val_fold["prediction"] == val_fold["after"]).mean()
print(f"Validation Accuracy: {val_accuracy:.6f}")

# Prepare test predictions — test data has no class column
test_pred = []
for _, row in test.iterrows():
    before = row["before"]
    # Since test has no class, directly use global mapping
    pred = token_to_norm_global.get(before, before)
    test_pred.append(pred)

test = test.copy()
test["after"] = test_pred

# Create submission file with correct id format: sentence_id_token_id as string
submission = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "id": test["sentence_id"].astype(str) + "_" + test["token_id"].astype(str),
        "after": test["after"],
    }
)

# Save submission
submission.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)

# Final validation metric
print(f"Final validation accuracy: {val_accuracy:.6f}")
